g.aria-label: Bae Ambua and Datu Mangoranda: either may be the sibling of Mampay; identity unresolved
g.title: Family account from a family informant: Bayango Gandamasir is a full first cousin of all children of Bae Ambua. Mampay may be a sibling of either Bae Ambua or Datu Mangoranda; which person is not yet known.

g.aria-label: Kararatan and the listed children of Bae Ampua / Ambua
g.title: Kararatan is included with Tantowaraga and the other listed children of Bae Ampua / Ambua, according to Alicasan’s account. Spouses and descendants remain outside the sub-box. Zolaika’s separately reported cousin relationship remains a family-account note.

g.aria-label: Mga anak at inapo ni Sayyidna ayon sa Gogodan sa Binidayan at Ameroden sa Bayang, Ontay & Marogong.Net
Tabonawan ancestry in Ameroden sa Bayang; identity match with Tabunawan remains tentative
g.title: Ameroden sa Bayang: paternal side Kadi → Paki → unnamed child of Paki → Tabonawan; maternal side Tuan → Amai Makapondag + Bagur → Babaida → Tabonawan. Bagur’s parents are Inai Manoyogun and Toron Zaman. The source does not explicitly identify this Tabonawan as Usman Imam’s father.
Paki. Source: Ameroden sa Bayang, Ontay & Marogong.Net.

path.title: Magkapatid sina Alicasan at Punda
Mampay may be a sibling of either Bae Ambua or Datu Mangoranda. This line connects to their shared group, not to one identified person. According to the family account; unresolved.
Usman and Mamadra are siblings · Alicasan account
Mamadra and Calanda Ginaronai are half-brothers according to the corrected Alicasan account. The shared parent remains unspecified.
Usman’s mother and Samurong are maternal cousins; common ancestors unknown · Alicasan account

Mohamad Ali Dimaporo and Calanda Ginaronai are reported second cousins in the family account. Their shared ancestors and connecting ancestry are not yet identified. This refers to Mohamad Ali Dimaporo (chart-132), not the earlier Sultan Dimaporo (chart-126).
Kararatan is reported as another child in the Ambua–Mangoranda family and sibling of Tantowaraga, according to Alicasan. Parentage remains a family-account claim.
Kararatan became Punda’s spouse, according to Alicasan.
Bayango Gandamasir and this family group: full first cousins according to Alicasan. This is a reported cousin relationship, not a parent–child link.
The shared partnership line between Kararatan and Punda branches to their child Ebra, according to the Alicasan account.

g.title: Bayango Gandamasir, pangalan sa legal na dokumento. Est. c. 1915–1925. Anak nina Mampay at Gandamasir at buong pinsan nina Sultan Hadji Nor at Tantowaraga ayon kay Alicasan. According to Alicasan, November 9, 2026, Bayango Gandamasir and Calanda Ginaronai are second cousins through the Digadong family. Their common ancestor and intervening ancestry have not yet been identified; this is a reported family relationship, not a calculated or independently verified kinship result. Names and descendant parent–child links: legal documents, including birth certificates. Oral accounts are separately attributed.

g.data-source-facts: Legal documents, including birth certificates, are the stated basis for the names and parent–child relationships from Calanda and Bayango through their descendants. Separate oral accounts about earlier ancestors, cousin relationships and historical events remain attributed to Alicasan.

g.title: Calanda Ginaronai, baybay sa legal na dokumento. Isinusulat ding Calanda Guinaronai. Tinatayang ipinanganak c. 1905–1930, batay sa kapanganakan ng anak na si Alicasan noong 1949. Asawa ni Bayango. According to Alicasan Calanda, Calanda Ginaronai travelled to Manila to sell peanuts. The date, route, vessel and length of stay are not yet known. This oral account is open for research in passenger lists, port or shipping records and other relevant archives; no matching record has yet been identified. According to Alicasan, November 9, 2026, Bayango Gandamasir and Calanda Ginaronai are second cousins through the Digadong family. Their common ancestor and intervening ancestry have not yet been identified; this is a reported family relationship, not a calculated or independently verified kinship result. Names and descendant parent–child links: legal documents, including birth certificates. Oral accounts are separately attributed.

g.aria-label: Tabunawan · father of Usman Imam · sixth-generation descendant · Kawashima Midori
g.title: Tabunawan / Tabonawan: one person according to family identification. Ancestry is from Ameroden sa Bayang; fatherhood of Usman and mosque role are recorded in Kawashima’s commentary. The cross-source identity match is supplied by the family.

g.data-source-facts: Names Tabunawan as Usman Imam’s father and village mosque imam, and describes Tabunawan as Sayyidna’s sixth-generation descendant. Estimated birth dates are not recorded by this source.
g.title: Kawashima Midori — Names Tabunawan as Usman Imam’s father and village mosque imam, and describes Tabunawan as Sayyidna’s sixth-generation descendant. Estimated birth dates are not recorded by this source.

g.data-source-facts: Ameroden lists Tabonawan, Imam sa Binidayan, as a child of Babaida and an unnamed child of Paki. Identification with the research Tabunawan follows the family account.
g.title: Salsila — Ameroden lists Tabonawan, Imam sa Binidayan, as a child of Babaida and an unnamed child of Paki. Identification with the research Tabunawan follows the family account.

g.aria-label: Asawa ni Tabunawan · ina ni Usman Imam · mula sa Bayang
g.title: Provisional birth range c. 1898–1923: inferred solely for layout by subtracting assumed parental age 20–45 from Usman’s 1943 birth year. Not a recorded birth date or a statement by Kawashima; row alignment does not prove contemporaneity.

g.data-source-facts: Describes Usman’s unnamed mother as coming from Bayang. The estimated birth range is a separate layout assumption.
g.title: Kawashima Midori — Describes Usman’s unnamed mother as coming from Bayang. The estimated birth range is a separate layout assumption.

g.aria-label: Usman Imam Sheik Al-Aman · son of Tabunawan
g.title: Usman Imam Sheik Al-Aman. Full name listed in Journal of Sophia Asian Studies 22 (2004), pp. 173–195. Alignment with Alicasan is for diagram layout, not proof of the same generation.

g.data-source-facts: Identifies Usman Imam, his 1943 birth year, father Tabunawan and unnamed mother from Bayang. The sibling link to Mamadra is a separate family account.
g.title: Kawashima Midori — Identifies Usman Imam, his 1943 birth year, father Tabunawan and unnamed mother from Bayang. The sibling link to Mamadra is a separate family account.

g.aria-label: Mamadra · half-brother of Calanda Ginaronai · sibling of Usman Imam
g.title: Mamadra and Calanda Ginaronai are half-brothers in the corrected Alicasan family account. Mamadra and Usman Imam are siblings. Their shared parent is not yet identified.

g.data-source-facts: Mamadra’s sibling relationship with Usman Imam and half-brother relationship with Calanda Ginaronai follow Alicasan’s account, November 2026. These connections are not attributed to Kawashima or the salsila.
g.title: Alicasan · November 2026 — Mamadra’s sibling relationship with Usman Imam and half-brother relationship with Calanda Ginaronai follow Alicasan’s account, November 2026. These connections are not attributed to Kawashima or the salsila.

g.aria-label: Kararatan · reported sibling of Tantowaraga, spouse of Punda and biological parent of Ebra · according to Alicasan
g.title: According to Alicasan: Kararatan is reported as a sibling of Tantowaraga, became Punda’s spouse, and is Ebra’s biological parent. This account differs from the earlier salsila attribution of Ebra to Tantowaraga; both accounts remain identified.

g.aria-label: Ebra, child of Punda and Kararatan according to Alicasan; identity with the salsila Ebra is unverified
g.title: Ebra, child of Punda and Kararatan. Reported full first cousin of Mohamad Ali Calanda and his siblings, according to the family account. Kept separate from the Ebra listed under Tantowaraga; whether those two records refer to the same person remains unverified.

Al-Hur (al-Hūr; フール), mother of Sayyidna. In Usman Imam’s lecture, she instructed her twelve-year-old son to travel to Mecca for pilgrimage and study. Source: Sophia record 2005239, section I.1. Saved excerpt and source details: docs/references/kawashima-usman-imam-record.html. Indexed text checked; PDF not visually verified.

g.data-source-facts: Al-Hur (al-Hūr) is named as Sayyidna’s mother in Usman Imam’s lecture, section I.1, translated by Saito Mitsuko with notes/commentary by Kawashima Midori. Sophia repository record 2005239.
